rows.derivation: Five sequential FDs cover every arm of the format: FA 'BLOCK CONTAINS 2 RECORDS', FB 'BLOCK 100' (no CONTAINS, no unit word = CHARACTERS), FC 'BLOCK CONTAINS 10 TO 100 CHARACTERS', FD2 'BLOCK 10 TO 20 RECORDS' (SR1 integer-2>integer-1 met), FE no clause. All legal so the program compiles; per the documented inert claim (A.3 5) each file written with three 8-char records reads them back in order then AT END -> lines FA=..0001,..0002,..0003,END etc.
citations: cite.py --check 13.18.10.2 "BLOCK CONTAINS" -> OK §13.18.10.2 (General format)
cite.py --check 13.18.10.1 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause specifies the size of a physical record." -> OK §13.18.10.1
cite.py --check 13.18.10.3 "If integer-1 is specified, integer-2 shall be greater than integer-1." -> OK §13.18.10.3 1)
cite.py --check A.3 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause has no effect if the operating environment does not support the required features" -> OK §A.3 5)
rows.notes: Lines FA..FD2 pin the format (compiling each arm is the observable). Also passes at --std 85 (the clause exists unchanged in 85; row editions start at 2002, so the golden is filed in 2002). Trailing spaces in the DISPLAY of a PIC X(40) line are ignored by the runner.

rows.derivation: GR4 gives integer-2 (alone) as exact size, and integer-1/integer-2 as min/max physical-record size. Under the documented inert claim no runtime behaviour reads either; the only compile-time consequence (ordering) is SR1, a separate row.

rows.derivation: Receivers sized exactly to each literal. B"0101"->Q1=[0101]; B'0110'->A1=[0110] (GR1/GR3); BX"A5"->QX=[10100101]; BX'3C'->AX=[00111100] (GR5/GR6); VALUE B'1'->VQ=[1]; VALUE BX'F'->VX=[1111]. B"", B'', BX"", BX'' are zero-length (GR4/GR7) and MOVE treats a boolean zero-length literal as ZERO (§14.9.25.4 GR3) over a B"1111" preset -> Z1..Z4=[0000].

rows.derivation: Pins the documented determination (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-16): a non-COBOL target is not located -> GR3b EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND -> GR3h 1 ON EXCEPTION. CALL "Cobol.Net.Runtime" (non-COBOL .NET assembly always present beside the program), CALL identifier 'System.Runtime', CALL "Antlr4.Runtime.Standard" -> T1/T2/T3=NOT-LOCATED. Control: CALL "L1C02F" (COBOL program of the run unit) -> SUB, then GR3i NOT ON EXCEPTION -> T4=CALLED.
citations: cite.py --check A.1 "CALL statement (calling a non-COBOL program). This item is required." -> OK §A.1 16)

cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "If the called program is a COBOL program, its execution is described in 14.2, Procedure division structure; otherwise the execution is defined by the implementor." -> OK §14.9.4.4 3) [g]
cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "If the program cannot be located or identifier-1 references a zero-length item, the EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND exception condition is set to exist." -> OK §14.9.4.4 3) [b]

cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "If the exception condition is any of the EC-PROGRAM or EC-EXTERNAL exception conditions and an ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified in the CALL statement, control is transferred to imperative-statement-1." -> OK §14.9.4.4 3) [h]
cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "otherwise, control is transferred to the end of the CALL statement or, if the NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2." -> OK §14.9.4.4 3) [i]
rows.notes: Pins a documented choice ('The same at every edition'); also passes at --std 2023 apart from the COBOLNET0903 ARCHAIC warning on EXIT PROGRAM (stderr), which is why the golden lives in 85 only. cite.py resolves GR3 sub-items only to '3)'; the letter is given in brackets. T1 is discriminating in any environment (the runtime dll must be present to run); T3 depends on Antlr4 dll beside the compiler (present in bin/Debug).

rows.derivation: No >>CALL-CONVENTION in source, so GR1 applies COBOL; under GR2a/§8.3.2.2 2a the CALL/CANCEL literal is a COBOL word whose basic letters are case-insensitive (§8.1.3.2 3a), so "l1c02d", "L1C02D", "L1c02D" all map to PROGRAM-ID L1C02D whatever the implementor's mapping. Sub counts activations: CALL lower -> SUB-COUNT=1; CALL upper -> 2 (same program, state kept); CANCEL "l1c02d" cancels it (GR2 covers CANCEL) so the next CALL "L1c02D" finds it in initial state (§14.9.5.4 GR3) -> SUB-COUNT=1. A literal (case-sensitive) mapping would print NOT-FOUND lines or SUB-COUNT=3.

rows.derivation: Permissive ('may also be used by the implementor'): grants latitude, imposes no obligation. COBOL.NET uses one .NET managed calling convention and takes no linkage details from the directive (CONFORMANCE.md recognized-and-ignored directives). Declining the latitude has no observable.

rows.derivation: Alphanumeric twin of l1_char_national_locale_tie. PCS = ALPHABET LOC IS LOCALE. ORD(X"00")=ORD(X"01")=ORD(X"1F")=1 (O00/O01/O1F=001) shows the undefined-order tie (r2 branch 2) is reached. Documented determination (DOC-A.1-21): the lowest-coded member is returned, CHAR(1)=X"00"; read through a BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED REDEFINES (1-byte unsigned binary, DOC-A.1-207) -> C1=000; a second invocation returns the same character (r2 last sentence) -> C2=000. Returning X"01"/X"1F" would give 001/031.

rows.derivation: Three classes, H INHERITS J, J INHERITS I, I INHERITS H: every INHERITS operand is in its REPOSITORY (SR2), none is self (SR3), FINAL (SR5) or repeated (SR7); each operand inherits from the declaring class only INDIRECTLY, so SR4's indirect arm alone requires rejection. Control (J's INHERITS removed) compiles clean.
citations: cite.py --check 11.3.3 "Object-class-name-2 shall not inherit from object-class-name-1 directly or indirectly." -> OK §11.3.3 4)
cite.py --check 11.3.3 "Object-class-name-2 shall be the name of a class specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of this source element." -> OK §11.3.3 2)
rows.notes: Rejected at 2002/2014/2023 with 'error COBOLNET0820: class 'L1C02H': the INHERITS chain is cyclic through 'L1C02H' (ISO §11.3.2 — ...)'. COBOLNET0820 is a shared OO structural code (duplicate class, END CLASS/METHOD mismatch, cycle); .err holds the code only. The message cites §11.3.2 rather than §11.3.3 SR4 (adjudicator finding inherits-cycle-citation, still present). 85 not listed: OO does not exist there, so rejection would be for another reason.

Source is decoded to UTF-16, which represents every COBOL character, so the antecedent is false and no substitute graphic exists to observe.
